model_annotation: Figure 3(a) displays a line plot illustrating the loss values over the number of training steps for various model configurations. The x-axis, labeled "Training steps," uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 2.5 million steps, with tick marks appearing at regular intervals of roughly 500,000 steps. The y-axis, labeled "Loss," uses a logarithmic scale, spanning from 0.1 to 10, with tick marks at intervals of one order of magnitude. The plot contains five distinct lines, each representing a different model variant: the Vanilla model is shown as a solid black line with circular markers; the SepLLM(n=64) model is a dashed red line with square markers; the SepLLM(n=128) model is a solid green line with diamond markers; the SepLLM(n=256) model is a dashed blue line with triangle markers; and the SepLLM(n=512) model is a solid purple line with star markers. All lines begin at a loss value of approximately 1.0 at step 0 and exhibit a downward trend, indicating decreasing loss over training. The Vanilla model initially decreases rapidly before leveling off near a loss of 0.5. The SepLLM models show varying rates of decrease; SepLLM(n=64) decreases more slowly than Vanilla and reaches a lower final loss. SepLLM(n=128) and SepLLM(n=256) follow similar trajectories, decreasing steadily to a final loss around 0.35. SepLLM(n=512) shows the steepest initial decline but appears to plateau at a higher loss value than the other SepLLM variants.
